title: Embodied Neuro-symbolic AI: Making Robot Behavior Auditable, Safe, and Scalable
summary: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) end-to-end systems have driven major progress in robot learning, yet they still face persistent barriers to dependable real-world deployment. In practice, these models often exhibit brittle generalization under distribution shift (i.e., novel objects, layouts, lighting, or contact conditions), limited physical and causal reasoning, and inconsistent fine-grained motor control. Critically, many VLA pipelines offer limited ways to express and audit what a robot must not do, making it difficult to provide assurance in safety-critical settings. These limitations constrain scalability, maintainability, and trust when robots move beyond controlled demonstrations. We propose Embodied Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) AI: a deployment-oriented paradigm that integrates learned perception, planning and control with explicit, machine-readable background knowledge and formal constraints. By combining knowledge-guided perception, constraint-aware symbolic planning, and hybrid learning, Embodied NeSy AI enables robots to reason about their environment, adapt to new tasks, and provide auditable, machine-checkable compliance with safety and operational requirements, thus supporting scalable, trustworthy robot deployment.

AI.tldr: 针对端到端VLA系统在分布偏移下泛化脆弱、物理与因果推理有限、且难以表达和审计安全约束的问题，作者提出Embodied Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) AI 这一面向部署的范式，把学习式感知、规划与控制同显式、机器可读的背景知识和形式化约束结合，以支持可审计、机器可校验的安全合规。摘要为范式性论述，未报告任何定量结果或实验验证。
AI.motivation: 现有VLA端到端系统虽推动机器人学习进展，但在真实部署中仍存在持续障碍：分布偏移（新物体、布局、光照、接触条件）下泛化脆弱，物理与因果推理有限，细粒度运动控制不一致。更关键的是，许多VLA管线缺少表达和审计"机器人不得做什么"的手段，在安全关键场景难以提供保证，从而限制可扩展性、可维护性与信任。
AI.method: 输入是机器人在真实环境中的感知与任务情境（含新物体、布局、光照、接触条件等变化）。机制上不做纯端到端黑箱，而是把学习得到的感知、规划与控制同显式、机器可读的背景知识与形式化约束整合，具体由三部分构成：知识引导的感知、约束感知的符号规划、混合学习。输出是能够对所处环境进行推理、适应新任务，并对安全与运行要求给出可审计、机器可校验合规性的机器人行为。相对所述VLA基线的改变在于把安全与操作要求从隐式表示转为显式可读、可检查的约束与知识。

title: Hi3R-VLA: Grounding Semantics and Actions in 3D
summary: While recent vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly incorporate 3D geometry, how to effectively exploit it for precise and generalizable action prediction remains a central challenge. We introduce Hi3R-VLA, a 3D policy that grounds heterogeneous modalities - vision, language, and action - in explicit 3D geometry for robotic manipulation. Our model integrates spatially-aligned visual features and language conditioning into point cloud representations, enriching scene geometry with fine-grained, task-relevant semantics. It then anchors low-level control commands in the same 3D coordinate frame and uses 3D-RoPE enhanced action-to-point attention over coarse-to-fine point features to model geometric relationships between action targets and observed points. Our analysis demonstrates the importance of semantic fusion within 3D and spatial alignment between observations and actions. With fewer than 250M trainable parameters, Hi3R-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance on RoboCasa, RLBench, RoboTwin2, DexJoCo and DexSuite across diverse manipulation tasks and embodiments, from single-arm and dual-arm grippers to dexterous hands. Real-robot evaluations further demonstrate its effectiveness in the physical world. The model, code and dataset are publicly released at this https URL .

AI.tldr: Hi3R-VLA 将视觉、语言与动作统一嵌入显式 3D 点云坐标框架，用 3D-RoPE 增强的动作—点注意力建模动作目标与观测点的几何关系。作者称其以少于 250M 可训练参数在 RoboCasa、RLBench、RoboTwin2、DexJoCo、DexSuite 上达到 SOTA，但摘要未给出数值结果。
AI.motivation: 近期 VLA 模型虽越来越多地引入 3D 几何，但如何有效利用几何实现精确且可泛化的动作预测仍是核心难题。摘要指出需要解决语义融合与观测—动作空间对齐这两个问题。
AI.method: 输入为视觉观测、语言指令与点云表示。方法把空间对齐的视觉特征和语言条件注入点云表示，使场景几何携带细粒度、任务相关的语义；随后把底层控制指令锚定在同一 3D 坐标系中，并在由粗到细的点特征上使用 3D-RoPE 增强的动作—点注意力，以建模动作目标与观测点之间的几何关系。输出是机器人在该 3D 坐标系中给出的操作动作。相对基线的关键改变是：在显式 3D 几何中统一异质模态，并让动作与观测共享同一坐标框架，而非仅在 2D 视觉特征上附加几何信息。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该工作给出的思路是把 3D 几何作为视觉、语言、动作三种模态的共同落点，并用相对轻量（<250M 可训练参数）的策略覆盖多种本体。证据边界在于：摘要仅提供 SOTA 的定性声明与参数规模，没有数值指标、基线名称、消融规模，实机部分也只说"证实有效"而未给出任务与测量方式，因此无法据此判断提升幅度或跨本体泛化的强弱。摘要未报告世界模型相关内容。

title: FoveaWAM: Role-Aware 4D World-Action Modeling for Dynamic Manipulation
summary: To manipulate a moving object, a policy must predict the scene at the moment its action executes, yet every millisecond spent predicting pushes that moment further away. Scene-level forecasts are computationally expensive, whereas target-centric forecasts can omit nearby objects that affect contact. Our key insight is that what a policy must predict decouples by role: only the target's pose, which determines contact, requires millimeter precision, while the surroundings matter primarily through the clearance they leave and the motion they impart. We present FoveaWAM, a native 4D world-action model that allocates precision according to these roles. Specifically, it models the target's past and future motion as a metric SE(3) trajectory, the surroundings as sparse 3D flow, and relies on the current frame for everything static. This compact representation lets FoveaWAM act in 15.1 ms on one RTX 5090, about 10 times faster than video world-action baselines, leaving substantially less time for the scene to evolve before action execution. To evaluate each policy under its own latency, we introduce OnTimeBench, a dynamic manipulation benchmark in which the scene keeps moving while the policy computes. FoveaWAM reaches 82.1% success on OnTimeBench, 20.8 points above the strongest baseline, and also leads on DOMINO and real-robot tasks. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: FoveaWAM 把"该预测什么"按角色解耦：目标位姿用米制 SE(3) 轨迹、周围环境用稀疏 3D 流、静态内容交给当前帧，从而在单张 RTX 5090 上 15.1 ms 完成动作，作者称约为视频世界-动作基线的 10 倍快；OnTimeBench 成功率 82.1%，比最强基线高 20.8 个百分点。
AI.motivation: 操作运动物体时，策略必须预测动作真正执行那一刻的场景，但花在预测上的每一毫秒都会把那一刻推得更远。场景级预测算力昂贵；而只看目标的预测又可能漏掉影响接触的邻近物体——摘要正是以这一对矛盾作为切入点。
AI.method: 输入是当前帧、目标的过去与未来运动、以及周围环境；方法把目标运动建模为米制 SE(3) 轨迹，把周围环境建模为稀疏 3D 流，并让当前帧承载全部静态信息；输出是这种按角色分配精度的紧凑 4D 世界-动作表示，用于产生动作。相对摘要所述基线的改动在于"不做什么"：不生成场景级/视频级的稠密预测，因为只有决定接触的目标位姿需要毫米级精度，周边只需其留出的间隙与所传递的运动。作者还提出 OnTimeBench，让场景在策略计算期间持续运动，以便按每个策略自身的延迟来评测。
AI.result: 作者报告三个量化结果：单张 RTX 5090 上动作耗时 15.1 ms，约为视频世界-动作基线的 10 倍快；OnTimeBench 成功率 82.1%，比最强基线高 20.8 个百分点（proportion 之差，属百分点而非相对百分比提升）；在 DOMINO 与真实机器人任务上也领先。基线具体身份、仿真与实机结果的划分、任务数量、模型规模与训练数据，摘要均未报告，因此无法独立核验这 10 倍与 20.8 个百分点的对照条件。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与世界模型研究，本文给出的命题是：世界模型不必对整个场景同等精细，而可以按"决定接触的目标 vs. 提供间隙与运动的周边 vs. 静态背景"分层分配表征精度，从而把延迟压到动作执行前场景变化较少的窗口内。证据边界很窄——仅有自建基准 OnTimeBench 的 82.1%、延迟 15.1 ms，以及"在 DOMINO 和真机上领先"这一无数值的表述；摘要未报告消融、统计显著性、失败模式与真实机器人任务细节，故不能推及更强的泛化性或部署鲁棒性结论。
AI.core_method: 把目标位姿、周边运动与静态背景分别用米制 SE(3) 轨迹、稀疏 3D 流和当前帧表示，构成按角色分配精度的紧凑 4D 世界-动作模型以加快动作预测。

title: Ground, Guide, Act: Improving VLA Spatial Generalization with Multimodal Foundation Models
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models effectively learn action policies from robot demonstrations, but struggle to generalize to changes in object positions and task goals. General multimodal foundation models (MFMs) offer complementary scene understanding and spatial reasoning, but remain slow and unreliable for direct fine-grained control. To understand how MFMs can improve VLA spatial generalization, we conduct a systematic capability analysis across multiple VLA architectures using atomic-stage interventions, revealing that many failures stem from poor target grounding and global spatial routing, while local manipulation skills remain largely usable. Based on these findings, we propose MFM-VLA, a selective collaboration framework in which an MFM provides target grounding and spatial guidance, controllers execute free-space motion, and the VLA retains control over fine-grained manipulation. We fine-tune the VLA with action-chunk-level dense geometric captions and perturbed-state recovery data to improve local guidance following and recovery from unfamiliar handoff states. A development-calibrated capability router selects between direct VLA execution and MFM-assisted execution to avoid unnecessary intervention. Across LIBERO-PRO, ALOHA-Sim-PRO, RoboCasa365, and real-world chemistry tasks, MFM-VLA improves success rates by 14.9, 74.0, 3.6, and 30.9 percentage points, respectively, over the corresponding base VLA. The project page is available at this https URL

AI.tldr: VLA 在物体位置与任务目标变化下泛化差；作者用原子阶段干预分析定位失败主要来自目标 grounding 与全局空间路由，提出 MFM-VLA：MFM 提供目标 grounding 与空间引导、控制器执行自由空间运动、VLA 保留细粒度操作，并用稠密几何字幕与扰动状态恢复数据微调 VLA 及能力路由器。跨 LIBERO-PRO、ALOHA-Sim-PRO、RoboCasa365 与真实化学任务，成功率较对应 base VLA 分别提升 14.9、74.0、3.6、30.9 个百分点（作者报告）。
AI.motivation: VLA 模型能从机器人示范中学习动作策略，但难以泛化到物体位置与任务目标的变化。通用多模态基础模型具备互补的场景理解与空间推理能力，但对直接细粒度控制而言仍慢且不可靠，因此需要弄清 MFM 应如何介入 VLA。摘要未报告具体任务失败率或现有方法的量化差距。
AI.method: 输入是 VLA 与通用多模态基础模型（MFM）。作者先在多个 VLA 架构上做原子阶段干预，把任务拆成阶段来定位失败来源。据此提出 MFM-VLA 选择性协作：MFM 负责目标 grounding 与空间引导，控制器执行自由空间运动，VLA 保留细粒度操作控制；再用 action-chunk-level 稠密几何字幕与扰动状态恢复数据微调 VLA，以改善局部引导跟随和从陌生交接状态的恢复；最后用基于开发集标定的能力路由器在「直接 VLA 执行」与「MFM 辅助执行」之间选择，避免不必要的介入。输出是一套分工式的执行策略，而非单一端到端策略。相对基线是各任务对应的 base VLA。
AI.result: 作者报告：在 LIBERO-PRO、ALOHA-Sim-PRO、RoboCasa365 与真实世界化学任务上，MFM-VLA 成功率较对应 base VLA 分别提升 14.9、74.0、3.6、30.9 个百分点（百分点，非相对百分比）。能力分析方面，作者称许多失败源于目标 grounding 与全局空间路由不足，而局部操作技能基本可用。摘要未报告各基准的绝对成功率数值、样本量、随机种子或统计显著性。
AI.conclusion: 该工作主张：VLA 空间泛化的瓶颈较集中在目标定位与全局空间路由，因此让 MFM 只承担 grounding/引导、让控制器与 VLA 承担运动与细粒度操作的选择性协作，可能比用 MFM 直接控制更合适。证据限于摘要所述四个评测（三个仿真基准加真实世界化学任务）的成功率提升，其中真实世界化学任务 30.9 个百分点的实验规模与条件摘要未说明；延迟与效率收益摘要未报告，因此不能推断该方法解决了 MFM「慢」的问题。

title: Perception Is Enough, at the Right Scale: Scale-Adaptive Token Pruning for Vision-Language-Action Models

summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models must process continuous streams of visual observations, and the resulting computational cost limits real-time robotic control. While these semantics evolve over the course of manipulation, they remain relatively stable between consecutive frames. This continuity allows retention indices computed from the current observation to be applied at the next policy invocation, enabling token selection to run asynchronously with inference and reducing pruning overhead. title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
summary: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies Effect targets. A shared generation expert learns to jointly predict Effect and an executable action chunk through flow matching, and reuses the sampled pair to generate future video on demand. This allows the controller to execute actions without waiting for video synthesis. We train on more than 20,000 hours of heterogeneous embodied data, excluding unused chain-of-thought data, and accommodate dataset-specific joint, end-effector, and hand-pose representations. Our evaluation uses the Small (8B) configuration on all five benchmarks and additionally evaluates the Large (26B) configuration on RoboDojo. Experiments examine closed-loop manipulation across complementary benchmarks, and comparisons across multiple baseline policies show consistent improvements from Action Grounding.

title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?
comment: 34 pages (8-page main paper and 23-page supplementary material), 19 figures, 28 tables. Project page: this https URL
summary: Robots must often keep working after the world changes, as when a block moves or the camera shifts while the robot still acts on what it saw before. Recent work showed that one change during a task lowers success for every policy tested, but did not separate the effect of its timing from the cost of the changed world, or measure what it costs afterwards. We introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases on CALVIN's five-instruction chains, each with one change to the objects, the camera, the robot, or the instruction. Each case compares three runs that are identical until the affected instruction begins: one without the change, one with it in place from that moment, and one in which it arrives while the robot is moving. The second run against the first gives the cost of the changed world, and the third against the second the effect of meeting it mid-motion. On 1,526 held-out cases per policy, with hypotheses fixed in advance, each of ten released policies loses 4.4 to 9.9 percentage points on the affected instruction over the eight core changes. Whether timing matters depends on the change: one that alters what the robot sees costs 5.4 points less mid-motion than from the start, whereas a change to the scene itself or to the robot shows no detectable effect. Rewinding the robot to the start of the instruction removes the benefit for every policy; the stricter test we fixed in advance, that the rewound run then matches the second run, passes for three. The cost also outlasts the affected instruction: the change stays in place, and a policy that still completes that instruction is 5.0 to 16.8 points less likely to complete the next one.

title: Ada-BFM: Adapting Behavior Foundation Models for Humanoid Scene Interaction
summary: Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose humanoid control through pretraining on large-scale behavioral data. However, their proficiency in whole-body coordination does not readily extend to scene interaction, which requires adapting motion to scene-dependent geometric constraints and contact dynamics. To bridge this gap, we introduce Ada-BFM, a post-training framework that adapts pretrained BFMs for humanoid scene interaction. Ada-BFM augments the original architecture with a lightweight adapter, enabling interaction-specific adjustments while leveraging pretrained control capabilities. Rather than producing a separate controller for each task, the framework yields a shared model for each interaction domain, supporting diverse tasks involving terrain or object interaction. Extensive experiments in simulation and the real world demonstrate that Ada-BFM enables diverse scene interaction behaviors, accelerates learning compared with training from scratch, and largely preserves pretrained behavioral competence. These findings establish Ada-BFM as an effective and efficient approach to extending the capabilities of BFMs beyond their pretraining settings while retaining their strengths in general whole-body control.

AI.tldr: 预训练行为基础模型（BFM）擅长全身协调，却难以应对需要几何约束与接触动力学的场景交互；Ada-BFM 在预训练 BFM 上接入轻量适配器做后训练，为每个交互域产出一个共享模型，作者报告其在仿真与真实世界中支持多样场景交互、比从零训练更快、并基本保留预训练行为能力。

title: PoseVLN: Learning Geometric State Evolution for Vision-Language Navigation

summary: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to relate past experience, current spatial state, and future motion while following natural-language instructions. Recent approaches improve these capabilities through long-horizon memory, state-aware reasoning, and future prediction, yet these components are often modeled separately, leaving navigation state evolution insufficiently connected across time. We argue that camera pose provides a natural geometric representation for bridging past, present, and future states. Based on this insight, we propose PoseVLN, a pose-aware VLN framework that jointly learns navigation decisions and geometric state evolution. PoseVLN organizes visual memory and the current observation in an episode-relative coordinate frame, and jointly predicts the next K navigation actions together with a local $\Delta$Pose over the same horizon. The predicted $\Delta$Pose is composed with the current trajectory-level pose to obtain the future pose state, which is recursively propagated throughout navigation, forming a continuous geometric state evolution from past memory to future motion. Experiments on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE Val-Unseen splits demonstrate the effectiveness of explicitly modeling geometric state evolution, with PoseVLN outperforming the strongest compared baselines by 2.6 and 2.9 percentage points in success rate, respectively, using only single RGB observations.

title: Co-DRIS: Physics-Informed Predictive Belief and Variable-Impedance Learning for Reactive Catching under Coupled Uncertainty
summary: Reactive robotic manipulation is acutely sensitive to simultaneous sensing noise, measurement dropouts, joint execution errors, and contact parameter variations. While single-frame frameworks like Domain-Randomized Instance Set (DRIS) achieve strong robustness under isolated uncertainties (86.4%), they degrade severely when perception and actuation uncertainties co-occur (27.6% across 10 coupled stress scenarios) due to memoryless encoding and fixed high-stiffness PD control. We propose Co-DRIS + SuperMimic, a perception-action co-design framework coupling: (i) an inertial world-frame physics-informed world model combining exact ballistic kinematics with a zero-initialized contact residual to roll forward missing observations and accelerate training via zero-cost counterfactual dropout consistency; (ii) an action-conditioned dual-stream causal GRU belief encoder resolving the denoising-vs-lag deadlock; and (iii) phase-aware variable-impedance soft-catching that transitions the 7-DoF Franka Research 3 arm into an overdamped regime (zeta/zeta0 ~ 2.26x) at the torque layer. Under unbiased 3-seed tail evaluation on unseen throws (15,360 throws/scenario), our method achieves 89.6 +/- 0.4% on standard benchmarks (+10.5% on 4-sigma noise to 70.5%) and 66.6 +/- 0.5% across 10 coupled/dropout stress scenarios (+39.0% over DRIS; +30.4% on 50% dropout). We further validate impedance decoupling, causal contact triggering under +0.65 s flight-time shifts, and cross-task transfer to steel-plate ping-pong bouncing (87.5% to 100.0%) and FR3+Hand catching (+8.4% under 4x noise with 6-13% lower peak impact force).

title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming for Robot Foundation Models
summary: This paper demonstrates an approach for correcting failures of robot foundation models (RFMs) without additional data collection, demonstrations, or training. We apply weight-space programming (WSP), in which a language-model agent directly reads and writes a neural network's parameters, to a large, pre-trained vision-language-action policy. The idea is simple: many policy failures are not random but repeatedly land in the same recognizable stuck state, so if that state is visible in the model's internal activations, a small edit could trigger a corrective movement while leaving the rest of the model's parameters unchanged. A core design choice is where to write the edit: repurposing a few near-silent neurons in the action expert lets the edit switch on in situations associated with the failure and produce a corrective movement, such as lowering the gripper toward the target, that is specified directly rather than learned through training. Empirically, when applied to the pi0.5 policy in simulation, we find that edits to roughly 0.0002% of the parameters can improve success on recurring failures, including for a policy that was already fine-tuned on its task. Reversed and random edits indicate that the gains come from the intended behavior, and the approach works best when the failure situation is recognizable and a simple correction can address it.

title: Many Senses, One World: Learning Hierarchical Multimodal World Representations for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Bimanual dexterous manipulation relies on multimodal inputs that capture visual context and non-visual physical interaction cues for precise and coordinated control. To address the challenge of effectively integrating these modalities for policy learning, we propose HiMoDex, a two-stage framework centered on hierarchical multimodal world-state representations. In Stage 1, we pretrain a hierarchical representation network on the collected dataset of 1.19 million synchronized multimodal time steps. The network integrates visual context with tactile, force-torque, and audio cues into unified world-state embeddings. In Stage 2, we freeze the pretrained network and use its embeddings to condition a shared world-action transformer. The transformer jointly learns action generation and action-conditioned future-state prediction. Experiments across five real-world tasks show that HiMoDex achieves an average success rate of 78.7\%, representing an absolute improvement of 32.0\% over the strongest evaluated baseline. Extensive ablations validate the benefits of hierarchical representation learning and two-stage training. Failure analysis helps explain performance differences across variants. Code, data, and demos will be released at this https URL .

title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
summary: Large language model (LLM) coding agents can iteratively self-improve robot manipulation skills in simulation benchmarks, yet real-world tasks provide neither ground-truth success scorers nor resettable practice environments. Our key observation is that a single real demonstration simultaneously specifies scene geometry, defines the terminal success criterion, and serves as a physical reference trajectory for verifying world fidelity---all decoupled from the source robot's kinematics. We present {RESET}: we reconstruct a contact-rich world and derive a frozen read-only criterion from one demonstration ({R}ebuild); check that world against the demonstration by open-loop replay and silhouette consistency ({E}xamine); evolve modular white-box task graphs and skill code from per-node failure evidence ({S}elf-improve); deploy frozen code on real robots with zero runtime LLM calls ({E}xecute); and share the verified world and criterion with unseen robots without new demonstrations ({T}ransfer). On 8 manipulation tasks, each rebuilt from one real demonstration, RESET achieves 97% average success on unseen layouts in simulation, whereas zero-shot code reaches 27%, per-task fine-tuned pi0.5 policies 31%, and Diffusion Policy 50%; injecting reconstruction defects shows that practice tolerates many reconstruction errors, that geometric errors can still stall or mislead it, and that the check flags most of them while physical randomization covers the rest. Without any target demonstrations, 3 heterogeneous robots acquire the same task skills in the shared world: a robot with similar arms copies 95% of its skill functions unchanged from the source robot, while robots with different arms and hands write their own. In real-robot experiments, the resulting programs run on 4 robots and succeed in 80% of 280 trials.

AI.tldr: 用单条真机演示同时重建接触丰富的仿真世界、冻结成功判据并作为世界保真度的物理参照，再让 LLM 代码智能体从逐节点失败证据自我改进技能；8 个操作任务在未见布局的仿真中平均成功率 97%，4 台真机 280 次试验成功率 80%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：LLM 代码智能体可以在仿真基准中迭代自我改进机器人操作技能，但真实世界任务既没有真值成功评分器，也没有可复位的练习环境。作者的观察是，单条真实演示同时规定了场景几何、定义了终止成功判据，并可充当验证世界保真度的物理参考轨迹，且这一切与源机器人运动学解耦。
AI.method: 输入是每项任务的一条真实演示。方法分五步：Rebuild 从该演示重建接触丰富的世界并派生一个冻结、只读的成功判据；Examine 用开环回放与轮廓一致性把世界与演示做比对；Self-improve 依据逐节点失败证据演化模块化的白盒任务图与技能代码；Execute 把冻结后的代码部署到真机，运行时零 LLM 调用；Transfer 把已验证的世界与判据共享给未见机器人，无需新演示。输出是可在真机运行的操作程序，以及可跨异构机器人复用的共享世界与判据。
AI.result: 在 8 个操作任务上（每个都由一条真实演示重建），未见布局仿真中的平均成功率为 97%，对照为零样本代码 27%、逐任务微调的 pi0.5 策略 31%、Diffusion Policy 50%。注入重建缺陷的实验显示：练习过程能容忍许多重建误差；几何误差仍可能使其停滞或误导；检查步骤能标记出其中大部分，剩余部分由物理随机化覆盖。迁移方面，在没有任何目标演示的情况下，3 台异构机器人在共享世界中获得同一任务技能，其中臂部相似的机器人从源机器人处原样复制了 95% 的技能函数，而臂部与手部不同的机器人则自行编写。真机实验中，所得程序在 4 台机器人上运行，280 次试验成功率为 80%。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该工作提出一种把“真实演示”同时当作世界重建源、成功判据与保真度参照的范式，使 LLM 代码智能体在没有真值评分器和可复位环境的真实任务上也能自我改进，并让验证过的世界与判据跨异构本体复用。证据边界：所有数字均为作者自报且未经独立验证；摘要只说明仿真未见布局的平均成功率与真机 280 次试验的总体成功率，未给出逐任务结果、统计显著性、对照条件的完整细节，也未报告重建缺陷注入实验的量化指标。关于“零运行时 LLM 调用”仅在流程描述中出现，摘要未报告其延迟或成本数值。

title: RoboHarness-RL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for VLM-Based Robot Manipulation
summary: Agentic harnesses enable frontier vision-language models (VLMs) to manipulate robots through perception, planning, and control tools, yet achieving comparable performance with compact open-weight VLMs remains challenging. We present RoboHarness-RL, an agentic reinforcement learning framework for improving VLM-based robot manipulation through tool calls. Starting from supervised fine-tuning on successful teacher demonstrations, the VLM further improves through multi-turn reinforcement learning with task-outcome rewards, without relying on vision-language-action models or world action models. To support efficient multi-turn training, we develop LiteHarness, which uses hierarchical memory to keep interaction contexts compact while preserving task performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, RL raises success from 31.2% to 44.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and from 57.8% to 73.3% on LIBERO-Pro; these gains extend to randomized RoboTwin scenes unseen during training (26.4% to 38.0%). Behavioral analysis further shows that RL reduces repetitive-call rates by up to $4\times$, shortens successful executions, and improves recovery from negative feedback. Project page: this https URL

AI.motivation: 作者指出：智能体式 harness 能让前沿 VLM 通过感知、规划与控制工具操作机器人，但让紧凑的开源权重 VLM 达到可比性能仍然困难。因此需要一个不依赖 VLA 模型或世界动作模型的、面向紧凑 VLM 的智能体式训练方案。
AI.method: 输入是 VLM 与一组感知、规划、控制工具，模型通过多轮工具调用与环境交互完成操作任务。方法分两步：先在成功的教师演示上做监督微调，再用任务结果奖励做多轮强化学习，使模型学会何时调用哪个工具；训练信号来自任务成败，而不来自视觉-语言-动作模型或世界动作模型。为支撑高效多轮训练，作者设计 LiteHarness，用分层记忆压缩交互上下文、同时保持任务性能。输出是经过 RL 更新的、以工具调用方式执行操作策略的 VLM。
AI.result: 作者报告以 Qwen3.5-9B 为基座，RL 后 RoboTwin 2.0 成功率从 31.2% 提升到 44.0%，LIBERO-Pro 从 57.8% 提升到 73.3%；在训练中未见的随机化 RoboTwin 场景上从 26.4% 提升到 38.0%。行为分析显示 RL 将重复调用率最多降低 4 倍、缩短成功执行时长，并改善对负面反馈的恢复。摘要未报告真实机器人实验、参数量消融或与其他基线的逐项对比数值。

title: FabricBench: A Standardized Policy Benchmark for Bimanual Fabric Manipulation with a Contact-Driven Deformable Simulator
summary: Fabric manipulation challenges robot policies with changing geometry, self-occlusion, and contact, yet standardized evaluation remains focused on rigid objects. We introduce FabricBench, a benchmark for bimanual fabric manipulation with six tasks spanning garments, silk, and bags, 10,000 simulation-ready assets, and controlled tests of configuration and appearance generalization. Built on an open-source solver in Newton, our simulator enables stable bimanual grasping, holding, and release through contact forces, without artificial attachment. Redesigned cloth-rigid contact and bidirectional force coupling support interactions among robot arms, fabric, and free rigid objects, allowing a bag to support its contents and transmit their weight to the grippers. In a controlled grasp-hold-release evaluation, our solver succeeds in all 45 trials, compared with none for the tested baseline configurations. Evaluating six representative policies, including vision-language-action models and world action models, reveals substantial remaining challenges: the best policy achieves 77% average success, while no policy exceeds 36% on long-horizon T-shirt folding. Under the most deformed initial T-shirt configurations, success falls to 6-14% across policies, with larger drops than under the evaluated appearance shifts. Zero-shot deployment of $\pi_{0.5}$ on a real robot largely preserves task difficulty ordering across six tasks (Spearman $\rho=0.94$). These results establish FabricBench as a reproducible testbed for measuring fabric-manipulation capabilities and exposing limitations in configuration generalization. The project website is available at this https URL .

AI.tldr: 布料操作缺少标准化评测，作者提出 FabricBench：基于 Newton 开源求解器的接触驱动可形变仿真基准，含六类布料任务与 1 万个可仿真资产，并做配置/外观泛化受控测试。作者报告最佳策略平均成功率 77%，长时程 T 恤折叠无一策略超过 36%，最形变初始配置下降到 6-14%，真机 zero-shot 保持任务难度排序（Spearman ρ=0.94）。
AI.motivation: 布料操作因几何形状不断变化、自遮挡和接触而难以处理，但现有标准化评测仍主要面向刚体对象，缺少可复现的双臂布料操作评测平台。

title: ActiveBridge: Scaling Active Prior for Robots through Egocentric Perception-Interaction Modeling
summary: Robotics foundation models are now widely used for manipulation, and egocentric videos offer rich data for scaling. However, existing methods overlook the human active priors captured in egocentric videos, which limits performance in unstructured scenes. They act on given observations instead of actively seeking information as humans do. We propose ActiveBridge, a training framework that learns these human active priors and transfers them to robots through world-action modeling. We design a robot that actively controls its viewpoint through head actions to acquire the visual information needed for manipulation using a single head camera, without wrist cameras. During human training, an instruction-conditioned model jointly predicts future egocentric videos and synchronized head-wrist action trajectories, with head actions providing explicit supervision for active perception. Experiments show that ActiveBridge outperforms baselines on active manipulation tasks, while ablations demonstrate the benefit of joint head-wrist action supervision.

title: Ego2Real: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Visuo-Tactile Demonstrations
summary: Learning dexterous manipulation from egocentric human demonstrations offers a scalable path toward robot skill acquisition. Vision alone, however, provides limited information about physical contacts and the demonstrator's force intent, leading to ambiguities in interpreting hand-object interactions. Capturing human touch via tactile sensing is therefore crucial for reliable human-to-robot dexterous skill transfer. We present Ego2Real, a framework that leverages egocentric demonstrations and tactile gloves to transfer bimanual dexterous manipulation skills to robotic hands. Ego2Real incorporates tactile supervision at two complementary stages: (1) tactile-guided hand-object interaction reconstruction, which uses measured tactile signals to refine hand poses and contact geometry; and (2) contact-informed reinforcement learning, which translates human contact patterns into robotic contact rewards. By combining refined motion references with physical contact rewards during training, Ego2Real guides anthropomorphic robotic hands to emulate demonstrated contact behaviors while adapting to their own morphology and actuation. Experiments show that incorporating tactile supervision into both reconstruction and policy learning yields higher manipulation success rates, underscoring the importance of enriching egocentric demonstrations with tactile observations to improve their quality and transferability.

title: One Phase Is Enough: Sim-to-Real Transfer with Direct Visual Reinforcement Learning
summary: Sim-to-real reinforcement learning (RL) has enabled impressive robotic behaviors, yet deploying policies directly from vision remains challenging. A common approach first trains a teacher policy with RL using privileged state observations, then distills its behavior into a vision-based student via imitation. However, the resulting student can substantially underperform its teacher. Directly training visual policies with RL offers a promising alternative, but learning task-relevant visual representations from scratch can be sample-inefficient, making one-phase visual RL intractable. We propose DRIFT, a simple recipe for efficient one-phase visual RL using image observations available at test time. Our key insight is to use frozen, pretrained foundation vision encoders, allowing RL to focus on learning control from existing visual representations. Freezing the encoder avoids costly backpropagation through the vision backbone, while its pretrained representations enable real-world transfer from fast, rasterized simulation rendering. Under matched architectures, observations, and compute budgets, DRIFT outperforms two-phase distillation and achieves a 58.8% relative improvement in average real-world success rate across three manipulation tasks. Controlled simulation evaluations demonstrate that DRIFT's relative advantage grows from roughly 9% in-distribution to over 61% under out-of-distribution shifts, suggesting that stronger generalization contributes to superior real-world transfer. title: KeyMemVLA: Subtask-Guided Key Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
summary: Memory-dependent long-horizon manipulation requires vision-language-action (VLA) policies to infer task progress and recall evidence absent from current observations. Under a limited memory budget, the challenge is to retain history that resolves stage ambiguity and supports subsequent decisions. We present KeyMemVLA, a subtask-guided key memory framework based on progress indication and decision-evidence retention. A two-level annotation process selects subtasks satisfying either criterion and labels their final frames as keyframes to supervise online memory writes. A shared vision-language backbone jointly learns subtask, action, and keyframe prediction. At inference, the policy first predicts the current subtask from the instruction, visual context, and memory, then uses this semantic condition to predict actions and future memory-write positions. Actual observations are retained at the selected times during execution. We introduce KMBench to evaluate active memory retention for decisions across subtasks. Evaluations on RMBench-$M(n)$, RoboTwin-MeM, KMBench, and real-world manipulation tasks show higher average success rates than the compared baselines. Ablation studies and representation analysis support the roles of key memory and explicit task-progress semantics. These results highlight the value of coupling sparse key memory with online progress inference for history-dependent control.

title: PreWAM: Exploring the Design of Latent Future Prediction for World-Action Modeling
summary: World-action models combine action generation with future prediction, allowing visual transitions to serve as supervision for policy learning. Our controlled study of prediction spaces shows that spatially structured semantic features support better overall generalization under visual perturbations and make motion information more readily recoverable from learned predictive representations. Building on these observations, we introduce PreWAM, a world-action model that organizes future supervision around state changes in a prediction space defined by pretrained DINO features. Specifically, Residual World Prediction jointly learns source-relative changes and their resulting future states to emphasize dynamic information while preserving future-state semantics. Temporal-Scale Prediction conditions world queries on temporal distance to capture both short-term local motion and longer-horizon state evolution. These predictive objectives jointly shape a shared vision-language backbone with action supervision during pretraining and downstream policy learning. Experiments across the LIBERO benchmark family, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world robotic manipulation demonstrate strong manipulation performance and improved generalization and robustness under diverse distribution shifts.

title: SkillHarness: Execution-Aware Coordination with Plug-and-Play Skills for Long-Horizon Traversal
summary: Traversing complex terrain requires robots to coordinate diverse locomotion skills while adapting to unseen obstacles and changing environments. Although perceptive reinforcement learning enables agile locomotion, conventional multi-terrain locomotion rely on fixed policy, limiting adaptability and skill extensibility. Perceptual disturbances and unreliable skill transitions further challenge robust execution. To address these challenges, we propose SkillHarness, an execution-aware coordination framework that integrates a flexible, plug-and-play locomotion skill library. To enhance traversal robustness, we introduce a perceptive reinforcement learning approach that preserves task-relevant environmental references while continuously updating proprioceptive feedback, reducing sensitivity to perceptual fluctuations. A vision-language-guided Harness coordinates navigation and skill execution through event-triggered reasoning, geometric feasibility verification, and execution-phase constraints. By flexibly composing and extending available skills, SkillHarness adapts to unseen terrain and task combinations without retraining the locomotion policies. The framework further incorporates execution feedback and retrospective decision revision to improve skill selection and avoid inappropriate skill switching. We evaluate SkillHarness across diverse terrain configurations, perceptual disturbances, and multi-obstacle traversal tasks to assess its adaptability and reliability in long-horizon traversal.

AI.tldr: SkillHarness 提出一个执行感知的运动技能协调框架：用可插拔的技能库配合视觉语言引导的 Harness，通过事件触发推理、几何可行性验证与执行阶段约束来协调导航与技能执行，使机器人无需重训练运动策略即可组合、扩展技能以应对未见地形。摘要仅说明在多类地形配置、感知扰动与多障碍穿越任务上做了评估，未给出任何数值结果。

title: VG-GP: Uncertainty-Gated Visuo-Geometric Memory for Negative-Transfer-Resistant Grasp Adaptation
summary: Pretrained antipodal grasping networks generalize well to canonical shapes but frequently fail zero-shot on novel objects with irregular mass distributions, thin rims, or unfamiliar handles. While episodic experience memory adapts a frozen base policy without retraining, naive retrieval suffers from visual appearance bias, negative transfer from overriding working base grasps, and degenerate closed-loop acquisition. We present VG-GP, a plug-and-play Visuo-Geometric Gaussian Process memory framework for closed-loop $SE(2)$ residual grasp transfer. First, we fuse color-invariant surface-normal DINOv2 features, canonical $SE(2)$ gripper-aligned 3D local heightmaps, and contact-geometry descriptors under a product kernel with Automatic Relevance Determination (ARD) lengthscales learned strictly on source objects. Second, we model the joint posterior over the base grasp and candidate $SE(2)$ alternatives, overriding the base policy only when the joint-covariance Lower Confidence Bound (LCB) clears a risk-sensitive threshold. Third, an online counterfactual curation gate using single-record necessity and sufficiency interventions quarantines source experiences causing negative transfer. Fourth, we close the acquisition loop via Bayesian Expected Improvement (EI) over equal-budget $SE(2)$ probes. Across 42 disjoint YCB objects in ManiSkill3 (20 source, 12 development, 10 held-out test), VG-GP wraps a pretrained GR-ConvNet base policy and raises physical lift rate across all 22 unseen objects from 38.6% (34/88) to 53.4% (47/88) with zero regressions (+13 rescues, 0 losses; object-clustered 95% CI [+6.8%, +22.7%], exact McNemar $p = 0.00024$). On the 10 held-out objects, EI active acquisition reaches 45.0% (18/40 vs. 32.5% base, 5/7 of oracle headroom), achieves 55.0% probe divergence over passive fallback, and monotonically reduces epistemic uncertainty.

AI.method: 输入是三类互补描述：颜色不变的表面法线 DINOv2 特征、规范 SE(2) 夹爪对齐的 3D 局部高度图、接触几何描述子，在乘积核下融合，其 ARD 长度尺度严格只在源物体上学习。方法在此基础上学习基抓取与候选 SE(2) 备选的联合后验，只有当联合协方差的下置信界越过风险敏感阈值时才覆盖基策略；一个在线反事实筛选门用单记录的必要性与充分性干预，隔离会引发负迁移的源经验；采集环节用贝叶斯期望改进在等预算 SE(2) 探针上闭环推进。输出是闭环 SE(2) 残差抓取决策，以可插拔方式包裹预训练 GR-ConvNet 基策略，基策略本身不重训。

title: Disentangling Visual Dynamics for World Model Planning
summary: Visual world models enable planning through predictive latent states. However, entangled agent and exogenous dynamics can obscure task progress. Disentangling visual dynamics for planning requires addressing two challenges: 1) suppressing cross-factor interference while retaining useful information; and 2) linking factors to task-relevant signals, since stability alone does not ensure meaningful planning distances. Therefore, we introduce FactorWorld, a disentangled visual dynamics framework for world model planning. To separate agent and exogenous dynamics, we propose a Counterfactual Consensus Residual Factorizer (CCRF) guided by bidirectional counterfactual pairs. CCRF separates shared context from dynamic residuals, combining average and worst-partner constraints to suppress interference with state and motion supervision to retain useful information. To translate these factors into planning decisions, we introduce semantic routing to refine full-representation task predictions for state estimation, trajectory scoring, and task-adapted planning. Experiments on MiniGrid, MetaDrive, and CARLA show improved bidirectional factor stability across two backbones. On MiniGrid, factor routing raises mean SR from 78.80% to 82.40%. Across four continuous control tasks, including Push-T, FactorWorld achieves mean success rates ranging from 91.67% to 100% across tasks. These results demonstrate that combining decoupled visual dynamics with explicit tasks can significantly improve the planning capabilities of world models.

AI.tldr: FactorWorld 用双向反事实配对训练的分解器把视觉动力学拆成智能体与外源两部分，再用语义路由把因子接到任务预测上；MiniGrid 上平均 SR 从 78.80% 升到 82.40%，四个连续控制任务平均成功率 91.67%–100%。
AI.motivation: 视觉世界模型依赖预测性隐状态做规划，但智能体动力学与外源动力学纠缠在一起会遮蔽任务进展。作者提出该问题需要同时解决两点：抑制跨因子干扰但保留有用信息，以及把因子与任务相关信号关联起来，因为仅靠稳定性并不能保证规划距离有意义。摘要未报告更早方法的具体失败数值。
AI.method: 输入是视觉观测构成的规划场景；方法学习把潜在动力学分解为共享上下文与动态残差两部分。分解器 CCRF 由双向反事实配对引导，并用平均伙伴约束与最差伙伴约束抑制交叉干扰，同时用状态与运动监督保留有用信息。为使因子可用于决策，作者引入语义路由，用完整表征精化任务预测，用于状态估计、轨迹打分和任务自适应规划。相对所述基线的具体差异摘要未报告（仅说明“稳定并不等于有意义”这一动机）。

title: Duo: Towards Spatiotemporal Action Coordination in Bimanual Policies
summary: Bimanual manipulation requires each arm to perform distinct motions while coordinating with the other. Common flow-based robotic policies combine both arms' actions into one token per future timestep, giving attention distinct positions across time but not across arms. We introduce Duo, a simple but effective design that models spatial and temporal dependencies within one shared action head. Specifically, Duo separates both arms into two action tokens per timestep, allowing each arm's motion to interact via cross-arm attention during flow matching. On RoboTwin 2.0, Duo improves the overall success of all four base policies, from 0.45B to 3.62B parameters, with gains of 12.55 and 9.02 percentage points for FLOWER (0.89B) and $\pi_{0.5}$ (3.62B), respectively. Despite its compact size, FLOWER-Duo achieves the best randomized-generalization, precision, and memory scores on RoboDojo. In real-world tasks, it outperforms $\pi_{0.5}$ in both success rate and execution speed, while scaling effectively with increasing training data. To provide deeper insight into the design of Duo, we conduct systematic ablations on inter-arm coordination, action grouping, and token granularity, confirming that cross-arm attention drives the improvement while arm-wise interaction offers the best accuracy-compute trade-off.

AI.tldr: 双臂流匹配策略通常把两臂动作压成每个时间步一个 token，Duo 改为每臂一个 token 并在 flow matching 中做跨臂注意力。在 RoboTwin 2.0 上，四个基座策略（0.45B–3.62B）成功率全部提升，FLOWER 提升 12.55 个百分点、π0.5 提升 9.02 个百分点。
AI.motivation: 现有基于 flow 的机器人策略把两臂动作合并为每个未来时间步一个 token，注意力因此只能在时间上区分不同位置，无法在臂维度上区分，双臂之间的空间依赖没有被显式建模。
AI.method: 输入仍是双臂动作序列，但不再压成每时间步一个 token，而是在同一个共享 action head 内为每个时间步拆成两个动作 token（每臂一个），在 flow matching 过程中让两臂动作通过 cross-arm attention 相互交互，最终输出双臂动作。相对基线（单 token 合并双臂）的改动仅在于动作分组与注意力交互方式。作者用关于臂间协调、动作分组与 token 粒度的消融来检验该设计。
AI.result: RoboTwin 2.0 上，Duo 提升全部四个基座策略（0.45B–3.62B 参数）的整体成功率，其中 FLOWER（0.89B）提升 12.55 个百分点、π0.5（3.62B）提升 9.02 个百分点。RoboDojo 上，较小的 FLOWER-Duo 取得最佳的 randomized-generalization、precision 与 memory 分数（摘要未给数值）。真实世界任务中，其在成功率与执行速度上均优于 π0.5，并随训练数据增加而有效扩展（摘要未给数值）。消融显示跨臂注意力是提升来源，arm-wise interaction 在精度–算力权衡上最优。
AI.conclusion: 该工作表明双臂策略的收益可以来自动作表示层面的细小改动：把臂维度显式拆成 token 并在其中做交互，比单纯增大模型规模更划算。但摘要只给出 RoboTwin 2.0 上的百分点增益，RoboDojo 与真实世界结果均为定性描述，尚无具体数值或统计检验，故不能据此判断该设计在更广泛任务上的稳健性。

title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
summary: Time is a fundamental dimension of robotic intelligence: a robot may fail despite physically correct actions if it acts outside a valid time window, responds too slowly to an event, or fails to meet required throughput. Yet existing robotic benchmarks primarily emphasize spatial correctness and logical task completion, largely overlooking the temporal constraints of real-world applications. We present RoboClock, a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation featuring 60 tasks across five application domains. Mirroring these failure modes, RoboClock structures tasks around three types of temporal constraints: Temporal Window, Event-Reactive, and Throughput. Furthermore, RoboClock incorporates a Latency-Aligned evaluation protocol that continuously advances environment time during model inference and control-interface delays, paired with time-sensitive metrics. Evaluating over 30 methods, we find that the best-performing approach is the trained VLA, yet it achieves only 8.3% temporal success even on Easy-level tasks, with persistent challenges in generalization and transfer. These findings reveal fundamental limitations in current robotic systems and highlight the need to jointly optimize physical competence, temporal reasoning, and execution latency.

AI.tldr: 现有机器人基准侧重空间正确性与逻辑完成，忽视真实应用的时间约束；RoboClock 提出覆盖五个应用域、60 个任务的时间感知操作基准，用"延迟对齐"评测在推理与控制延迟期间持续推进环境时间；作者报告在 30 多个方法中最佳的已训练 VLA 在 Easy 级任务上时间成功率仅 8.3%。
AI.motivation: 机器人即使物理动作正确也可能失败：动作落在有效时间窗之外、对事件响应过慢、或达不到所需吞吐。作者指出，现有机器人基准主要强调空间正确性与逻辑任务完成，基本忽视真实应用中的时间约束。
AI.method: 输入是分布在五个应用域的 60 个机器人操作任务。关键改动有两处：一是按三类时间约束组织任务（Temporal Window、Event-Reactive、Throughput）；二是引入 Latency-Aligned 评测协议，在模型推理与控制接口延迟期间持续推进环境时间，并配合时间敏感指标。产出是一个统一基准与评测协议，用于给出时间敏感指标（如时间成功率）。相对参照是现有偏重空间正确性与逻辑完成的机器人基准（摘要未给出具体基线名称与配置）。
AI.result: 作者报告评估了 30 多种方法：表现最好的是已训练的 VLA，但在 Easy 级任务上时间成功率仅 8.3%，泛化与迁移仍是持续挑战。摘要未报告其他方法的数值、未给出统计显著性，也未说明评估在仿真还是真机上进行。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能而言，该结果提示时间维度可能是当前操作策略的主要瓶颈之一，作者据此主张把物理能力、时间推理与执行延迟联合优化。证据边界：可用数值只有 8.3% 这一项，来自作者在自建基准上的评估，未经独立验证；摘要未说明仿真/真机、硬件平台、延迟量级与样本规模。

title: Reading Geometric Anchors: Viewpoint Generalization in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation with RGB-Only Deployment
summary: Moving the camera changes where objects appear in an image, challenging RGB-based imitation learning. A common strategy pairs synthesized views with the same demonstrated action, but ignores supporting physical correspondence across views. By predicting depth with camera calibrations, 3D policies may handle it yet suffer the issue of varied observed point sets. To address these limitations, we propose ReGeoAnch, a geometry-anchored imitation learning framework for viewpoint generalization. Specifically, we build global anchors in the robot base frame and local anchors in the gripper frame, providing shared physical references across viewpoints. Furthermore, Decoupled Appearance-Guided Geometric Readout uses Point-to-Anchor Aggregation (PAA) to obtain comparable and stable geometry around anchors beyond pointwise correspondence. A controllable and decoupled information flow, Anchor-to-Policy Readout (APR), leverages complementary visual and geometric information and supports viewpoint generalization: view-dependent appearances are queried by view-invariant robot state to select task-relevant anchors, with geometric values alone to form the final readout. We further introduce Cross-View Readout Consistency to align the directions of policy readouts from paired source and synthesized target views. Experiments on 12 manipulation tasks across MetaWorld and ManiSkill3 demonstrate improved viewpoint generalization over baseline policies.

AI.tldr: 针对RGB模仿学习在相机视角变化下退化的问题，ReGeoAnch在机器人基座系与夹爪系建立几何锚点，并解耦外观与几何信息流，作者称在MetaWorld与ManiSkill3的12个操作任务上视角泛化优于基线策略；摘要未报告任何数值。
AI.motivation: 相机移动会改变物体在图像中的位置，使基于RGB的模仿学习受挑战。常见做法是把合成视角与同一演示动作配对，但忽略跨视角之间的物理对应关系；用相机标定预测深度得到的3D策略虽可应对，却受观测点集变化的问题困扰。
AI.method: 输入为图像观测（源视角与合成目标视角）、机器人状态与相机标定。方法在机器人基座坐标系建立全局锚点、在夹爪坐标系建立局部锚点，作为跨视角共享的物理参考；PAA（Point-to-Anchor Aggregation）在锚点周围聚合，得到可比且稳定的几何量，而不再依赖逐点对应关系。APR（Anchor-to-Policy Readout）把信息流解耦：用视角无关的机器人状态去查询视角相关的外观以选出任务相关锚点，最终读出只由几何值构成。训练上另有跨视角读出一致性，令源视角与合成目标视角的策略读出方向对齐。输出是用于操作的动作策略，部署时使用RGB。相对所描述的基线（配对合成视角的增广、基于深度的3D策略），改动在于以锚点作为共享物理参考、将外观与几何显式解耦，并加入跨视角读出一致性约束。
AI.result: 作者报告在MetaWorld与ManiSkill3的12个操作任务上，视角泛化较基线策略有改进；摘要未报告任何数值、指标或提升幅度，也未给出基线的具体名称与实验条件。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能/世界模型而言，其思路是把视角相关的外观与视角不变的几何显式解耦，并用跨视角共享的几何锚点承载物理对应关系，为视角泛化的模仿学习提供了一种结构设计。但证据仅限于作者在摘要中的定性声明：无任何数值结果，也无真实机器人评测，无法判断改进幅度与适用边界。

title: Motion Chain of Thought: Disentangling Motion Semantics from Visual Appearance for Robotic Manipulation
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) aim to construct a unified architecture capable of understanding world state evolution and guiding action generation. However, existing visual branches focus on predicting static visual observation, rather than reflecting potential transition information that captures the evolution of world states under motion interactions. This leads to representational entanglement between high-level physical condition evolution and low-level action trajectory generation within the Action Model, creating a structural bottleneck while weakening the predictive capability of world evolution modeling for action generation. We propose PILOT (Physical Inference for Latent Optimized Trajectories), whose core Representational Deduction (RD) bridges this gap by integrating motion chain-of-thought (CoT) guidance as a native model capability. Specifically, RD aims to encourage the action branch to explicitly model potential state transition tokens, which are retained as CoT in the reasoning space to guide fine-grained motion trajectory. Experiments demonstrate that RD not only improves the success rate and generalization ability of WAMs in complex robotic manipulation tasks but also enhances the model's physical interpretability by decoupling high-level motion semantics from low-level trajectory details. Furthermore, the abundant state transition supervision signals introduced by RD effectively alleviate the sparse supervision in action generation, supporting data-efficient real-robot adaptation with reduced demonstration sets.

title: VLAs Execute, Code Recovers: 3D Skill Envelopes Bridge the Compositional Gap in Agentic Manipulation
summary: Composing frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) skills under an agentic planner promises scalable long-horizon manipulation without long-horizon demonstrations, yet strong atomic skills routinely fail at seams even under a correct plan. Standard remedies reset the robot's pose or draft entry conditions in language, missing the physical cause we uncover via causal interventions: even after re-homing, a frozen VLA rigidly retraces its habitual trajectory and collides with displaced scene residue, whether or not it can see it. We propose the Skill Envelope, a policy-measured 3D geometric precondition capturing the volume a frozen skill sweeps during successful executions. Exploiting the insight that the rigidity making a frozen skill fragile at seams also makes its trajectory predictable in advance, we expose each envelope as two classical 3D tools (CHECK to detect blocking residue and FREE to locate safe placement regions), establishing a division of labor where VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation and code repairs out-of-distribution states. On LIBERO-Goal with frozen $\pi_{0.5}$, our zero-failure envelope predicts collisions at 0.946 AUROC (0.944 from one RGB-D view) and beats frontier VLMs on seam readiness (0.902 vs. 0.793); using it for skill ordering and code repair lifts success from 82.8% to 92.3% on two-step seams and from 29.7% to 93.8% on drawer-bearing 3-4 step chains, matching privileged world reset. Together, these results show that reliable VLA composition hinges on measuring a policy's physical workspace rather than guessing preconditions in language. Ongoing work closes the loop with autonomous LLM orchestration, synthesized free-object recovery, and cross-policy evaluation on cluttered benchmarks and real hardware.

title: Learning World Models through Contrastive Identification of Actions
summary: Latent world models enable goal-directed planning from offline visual data, but prediction alone does not specify which action-related distinctions their representations should preserve. Inverse dynamics provides auxiliary supervision, yet squared-error action regression rewards additional information only through changes in the conditional action mean. We propose Contrastive Identification of Actions (CIA), which identifies the executed action among alternatives sampled from a history-conditioned behavior proposal. Comparing actions plausible in the same context targets information supplied by the next latent beyond history. Under exact behavior matching, we show that CIA can reward action information that leaves optimal inverse-regression error unchanged, and verify this distinction through a controlled learning example. CIA achieves higher planner-averaged mean success than the base world model and a regression inverse-dynamics baseline across five visual control benchmarks, without modifying the planner.

title: Any2Act: Scaling In-Context Robot Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrations
summary: Robot in-context learning (ICL) enables a policy to perform unseen tasks by following contextual demonstrations, without task-specific fine-tuning. This is increasingly valuable as large language models reasoning at low frequency can specify tasks through demonstrations and delegate high-frequency execution to such a policy. However, methods conditioned on human videos are bounded by scarce human-robot pairs, while those conditioned on robot demonstrations accept only one or two source types at limited scale. We present Any2Act, a foundation model for robot ICL. Our key insight is that a demonstration should be expressed in the camera layout and action space of the robot that performs it (the executor), not of whoever provided it (the demonstrator). This unified embodiment-grounded representation decouples learning to follow from admitting a new source. Any2Act learns to follow once, from robot-to-robot pairs that already take this form in 1.2M real trajectories spanning 10K tasks. Human videos, simulation, UMI, and other robots are then translated into this representation, and source-routed adapters trained on only a few hundred pairs each absorb the residual gap while the pretrained model stays frozen. For long horizons, a training-free tracker feeds only the demonstration window around the executor's progress, bounding the context and rolling back to redo failed steps. From a single demonstration, Any2Act achieves 57.5% success on unseen tasks without fine-tuning, exceeding VLAs fine-tuned on 50 demonstrations per task; other demonstrators retain 74-91% of the success achieved with the executor's own demonstrations.

AI.tldr: 为让机器人策略仅凭上下文演示完成未见任务，Any2Act 把任意演示统一改写为执行机器人的相机布局与动作空间，并用冻结的基础模型加少量来源路由适配器吸收新来源差异；作者报告单条演示、无需微调时未见任务成功率 57.5%，超过按每任务 50 条演示微调的 VLA。
AI.motivation: 机器人上下文学习（ICL）的价值在于不做任务特定微调、仅靠上下文演示完成未见任务，并可与低频推理的大语言模型分工（大模型指定任务、策略高频执行）。但现有方法受数据瓶颈限制：以人类视频为条件的方法受限于稀少的人-机器人配对；以机器人演示为条件的方法只接受一两种来源类型，且规模有限。

title: LeanWAM: Learning Latent World Action Models from Frozen Video Models
summary: World action models (WAMs) typically adapt large pretrained video generators to jointly predict future observations and robot actions, incurring substantial training and deployment costs. However, it remains unclear which future representations a policy actually needs and how compactly they can be represented. Our probing study shows that complementary future representations can be compressed into a few tokens while retaining most of their action-decoding performance. Motivated by this finding, we introduce LeanWAM, a latent WAM that transfers video priors from a frozen video generator to a lightweight policy via two-stage training. In the first stage, a Future Extractor compresses observed transitions into 32 predictive tokens. These tokens condition the frozen generator and are jointly shaped by action, RGB, semantic, and geometric supervision, while a compact readout of the generator's hidden states supplies complementary world tokens. The second stage distills both representations into the policy, which learns to predict them from current observations while generating actions. With 1.4B parameters and no large-scale embodied pretraining, LeanWAM outperforms strong vision-language-action (VLA) and WAM baselines on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin~2.0. It predicts an action chunk in 25.1\,ms on an A100 GPU, 12.3--41.5$\times$ faster than representative WAMs. These results demonstrate that compact predictive supervision can transfer video priors to robust and efficient control.

AI.tldr: LeanWAM 把冻结视频生成器中的视频先验，通过两阶段训练迁移到一个轻量策略上：先用 Future Extractor 把观测转移压缩成 32 个预测 token，再把生成器的预测表征与世界 token 蒸馏进策略。作者报告其在 LIBERO、LIBERO-Plus、RoboTwin 2.0 上超过强 VLA 与 WAM 基线，并在 A100 上以 25.1 ms 生成一个动作块。
AI.motivation: 世界动作模型（WAM）通常需要适配大型预训练视频生成器来同时预测未来观测与机器人动作，训练与部署代价高。摘要指出一个尚未明确的问题：策略究竟需要哪些未来表征，以及这些表征能被压缩到什么程度。作者的探测研究给出动机性发现——互补的未来表征可以压缩到少量 token，同时保留大部分动作解码性能。
AI.method: 输入是观测到的转移（transitions）与当前观测。第一阶段：Future Extractor 把观测转移压缩为 32 个预测 token；这些 token 用于条件化冻结的视频生成器，并同时受动作、RGB、语义与几何监督塑造；生成器隐状态的紧凑读出提供互补的“世界 token”。第二阶段：把这两类表征蒸馏进策略，策略学习从当前观测预测它们，同时生成动作。相对所述基线的变化在于：不微调大型视频生成器，而是只训练轻量的压缩/读出与策略，从而把视频先验转移到 1.4B 参数、且未做大规模具身预训练的策略中。
AI.result: 作者报告：在 1.4B 参数、无大规模具身预训练的条件下，LeanWAM 在 LIBERO、LIBERO-Plus 与 RoboTwin 2.0 上超过强 VLA 与 WAM 基线，但摘要未给出成功率等具体数值；在 A100 GPU 上预测一个动作块耗时 25.1 ms，比代表性 WAM 快 12.3–41.5 倍（相对倍数，非百分点）。探测研究层面，摘要称互补未来表征可压缩为少量 token 并保留大部分动作解码性能，未报告具体指标值。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能与世界模型研究的含义是：策略可能并不需要完整的未来观测生成能力，少量压缩的预测 token 加紧凑世界 token 就足以把冻结视频模型的先验转成控制能力，并在效率上取得明显收益。证据边界：所有结论均为作者自报，摘要未给出基准数值、真实机器人实验、消融或统计显著性，因此“超过基线”的具体幅度与真实部署表现无法从摘要判断。

title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
summary: Agent-orchestrated robot systems combine the general reasoning capability of multimodal agents with the precise physical control of learned visuomotor policies. Yet such systems often fail at the moment of handoff: a policy is reliable only from a limited set of start states, while the agent may invoke it outside this region. We call this region the policy's handoff boundary. Existing whole-task policies typically have handoff boundaries that are narrow and difficult for an agent to characterize, making reliable coordination challenging. We propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning, which explicitly shapes and then expands the handoff boundary of a visuomotor policy. First, Boundary-Explicit Training fine-tunes the policy on contact segments with diverse start poses, yielding a wide and well-defined boundary that can be communicated to the agent through a simple handoff protocol. Second, Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement retrains the policy on curated successful system rollouts, extending the boundary toward earlier stages of each task and allowing the agent to hand over sooner with fewer language-model calls. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboDojo, our system outperforms the strongest baseline by over 26 percentage points, reaching 98.4% success in randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, while further reducing its API cost and execution time by 41.3% and 37.5%, respectively. These results suggest that the key to robust agent-policy orchestration lies not only in improving either component individually, but also in explicitly shaping the boundary between them.

AI.tldr: 论文指出多模态智能体与视觉运动策略的「交接」常因策略仅在有限起始状态集上可靠而失败，提出边界感知策略学习，先塑造再扩展该交接边界。作者报告在 RoboTwin 2.0 与 RoboDojo 上以超过 26 个百分点领先最强基线，随机化 RoboTwin 2.0 场景成功率 98.4%，并使 API 成本与执行时间分别降低 41.3% 与 37.5%。
AI.motivation: 作者提出的失败模式是「交接时刻」：策略只在一组有限的起始状态下可靠，而智能体可能在可靠区域之外调用它，这个区域被称为策略的 handoff boundary。摘要称现有的整任务（whole-task）策略其交接边界狭窄且难以被智能体刻画，导致可靠协同困难。摘要未报告该问题在真实机器人上的具体表现，也未给出失败率等量化证据。
AI.method: 输入是一个「多模态智能体 + 学习到的视觉运动策略」的编排系统，输出是一个边界被显式塑造并扩大的策略以及配套的简单交接协议。方法分两步：Boundary-Explicit Training 在带有多样起始位姿的接触片段（contact segments）上微调策略，得到宽且定义良好的边界，从而可用简单协议向智能体传达；Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement 用筛选后的成功系统 rollout 重新训练策略，把边界向任务更早阶段扩展，使智能体能更早交接、减少语言模型调用。摘要在 Baseline 中只写「最强基线」，未指明其具体方法。
AI.result: 作者报告在 RoboTwin 2.0 与 RoboDojo 两个基准上，优于最强基线超过 26 个百分点（percentage points，而非相对百分比），在随机化 RoboTwin 2.0 场景达到 98.4% 成功率；同时使 API 成本与执行时间分别降低 41.3% 和 37.5%（相对下降，摘要未明确下降的基数与对比对象是基线还是自身）。摘要未报告真实机器人实验、任务数量、消融、统计显著性、延迟绝对值或硬件信息。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能体与策略协同而言，该工作提示性能瓶颈可能不只在单个组件，而在两者之间的可交接区域：把边界显式化并扩大，可让智能体更早移交控制并减少语言模型调用。证据边界有限——所有数值均为作者自报，且仅出现在 RoboTwin 2.0 与 RoboDojo 的摘要描述中；摘要未声明真实机器人部署，也未提供边界刻画协议的细节与消融证据，因此边界机制各部分的独立贡献无法从摘要判断。
AI.core_method: 先在多样起始位姿的接触片段上微调策略以塑造清晰可传达的交接边界，再用筛选出的成功系统 rollout 重训策略把该边界扩展到任务更早阶段。

title: EgoLoAF: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations with Hand-Object Affordances
summary: Training humanoid vision-language-action (VLA) models relies heavily on costly real-robot teleoperation. Recent efforts convert egocentric human demonstrations into humanoid training data. However, most methods still require wearable motion trackers and leave important hand-object interaction cues implicit. Many also mix in real-robot teleoperation data for VLA post-training. These dependencies limit scalable data collection, while implicit interaction cues make precise contact harder to learn. To overcome these limitations, we propose EgoLoAF, the first paradigm to derive all training data for humanoid loco-manipulation directly from egocentric demonstrations without wearable motion trackers. We post-train the VLA on the converted data alone, without real-robot teleoperation demonstrations, and use explicit hand-object interaction cues to guide action generation. Specifically, to obtain humanoid action targets, we estimate torso motion from recorded camera poses and reconstruct both hand trajectories from video. From the same recording, we use each hand's current pose relative to the object to represent hand-object affordances. During post-training, we inject these affordances into the action expert through cross-attention while keeping the vision-language backbone frozen. Additionally, we release 128,400 egocentric demonstration episodes spanning 1,000 hours and 1,284 tasks, together with converted humanoid action trajectories and rendered robot-view observations. Across four real-world tasks, EgoLoAF nearly achieves teleoperation performance (73.1 vs. 74.4 in mean Task Progress Score), while achieving a mean 4.03 times improvement in data-collection efficiency.

AI.tldr: 针对人形 VLA 训练依赖昂贵遥操作、已有第一人称数据转换多需穿戴式动作捕捉且手物交互线索隐式的问题，EgoLoAF 仅用第一人称演示生成全部训练数据（由相机位姿估躯干运动、从视频重建双手轨迹，并把"手相对物体的位姿"作为显式可供性注入动作专家），作者报告在四个真实世界任务上平均 Task Progress Score 达 73.1（遥操作为 74.4），数据采集效率平均提升 4.03 倍。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：人形 VLA 训练严重依赖代价高昂的真实机器人遥操作；已有把第一人称人类演示转为人形训练数据的方法，多数仍需穿戴式动作追踪设备，且把手-物交互线索留作隐式，导致精确接触更难学习；不少方法还在 VLA 后训练中混入真实机器人遥操作数据，这些依赖限制了数据采集的可扩展性。
AI.method: 输入是第一人称（egocentric）人类演示录像。方法先把录像转为人类动作目标：从记录的相机位姿估计躯干运动，并从视频重建双手轨迹；同时从同一段录像中取每只手相对物体的当前位姿，作为显式的"手-物可供性"表示。后训练阶段，这些可供性通过 cross-attention 注入动作专家（action expert），而视觉-语言主干保持冻结，VLA 仅在该转换数据上后训练。输出的产物包括：一个用于人形 loco-manipulation 的 VLA 策略，以及公开的 128,400 条第一人称演示回合、转换后的人形动作轨迹和渲染的机器人视角观测。相对摘要中描述的先前提法，其变化在于不使用穿戴式动作捕捉设备、后训练不混入真实机器人遥操作演示、并把交互线索由隐式改为显式注入。

title: Next-Manip: On-Demand Agent-Policy Collaboration for Robotic Manipulation
summary: General-purpose robotic manipulation requires task reasoning, failure recovery, and precise control, yet limited manipulation data make these abilities difficult to obtain from a single policy. Recent multimodal agents show promise in task reasoning and recovery but lack reliable fine-grained control and incur high inference cost, whereas learned policies provide efficient fine-grained execution but struggle beyond their learned skills. Although their complementary strengths suggest combining the two, doing so requires repeatedly deciding which executor should act as task demands change. Instead of relying on the agent for each decision, we present Next-Manip, an on-demand agent--policy collaboration framework that decouples executor allocation from costly agent inference. We propose an Agent Invocation Controller (AIC) that allocates control between the policy and the agent through a lightweight classifier of current execution demands. We further introduce Task Dynamics Context (TDC), which packages informative manipulation changes from in-context examples into compact task references to support both agent reasoning and executor allocation. Across two simulation benchmarks and real-world experiments, Next-Manip achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing agent inference costs.

AI.tldr: 单一策略难以同时具备任务推理、失败恢复与精细控制。Next-Manip 提出按需的智能体—策略协作框架，用轻量分类器决定何时调用多模态智能体、何时由策略执行。作者声称在两个仿真基准与真实实验中取得SOTA并降低智能体推理成本，但摘要未给出任何数值。
AI.motivation: 通用机器人操作需要任务推理、失败恢复和精确控制，而有限的操作数据使单一策略难以获得这些能力。多模态智能体在任务推理与恢复方面有前景，但缺乏可靠的细粒度控制且推理成本高；习得策略能高效细粒度执行，却难以超出已学技能。两者能力互补，但结合时需要不断判断当前应由哪个执行者行动。

title: CodeWAM: A Code World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Driving world models anticipate action consequences through representations of how the world evolves. For autonomous driving, these representations must capture both the surrounding scene and the ego vehicle's motion under a candidate plan. We propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that incorporates executable code as part of its world representation. Code represents ego dynamics by expressing how the vehicle state evolves under plan execution, while a learned visual model captures scene-dependent consequences. Executing the code produces a candidate-conditioned motion sequence, which is evaluated relative to the prior plan and recorded motion history. The resulting execution consequences and learned scene outcomes jointly represent the candidate's future, enabling the planner to assess both what a plan may lead to and how the vehicle transitions into that future. The selected plan becomes part of the next decision's execution context, linking successive choices within the model. CodeWAM achieves 93.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, 92.1 EPDMS on v2 navtest, and 50.6 EPDMS on NAVHARD. Further experiments demonstrate improved pairwise execution consistency and gains on Hydra-MDP and DrivoR without additional training, supporting executable code as a complementary representation for driving world models.

AI.tldr: CodeWAM 将可执行代码纳入驾驶世界模型的世界表示：代码刻画候选规划执行下自车状态的演化，学习式视觉模型刻画依赖场景的后果，二者联合表示候选的未来供规划器评估。作者报告 NAVSIM v1 navtest 93.6 PDMS、v2 navtest 92.1 EPDMS、NAVHARD 50.6 EPDMS（摘要未给出对比基线）。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，驾驶世界模型要通过"世界如何演化"的表示来预判动作后果；这类表示必须同时捕捉周围场景与候选规划下的自车运动。即需要同时回答"该规划可能导致什么"以及"车辆如何过渡到那个未来"，仅靠单一表示不足以覆盖这两方面。
AI.method: 输入是当前场景与候选规划，并与上一时刻规划、已记录的行驶历史相对照。机制上，方法把可执行代码作为世界表示的一部分：代码表达在规划被执行时车辆状态如何演化（自车动力学），学习式视觉模型则负责捕捉依赖场景的后果。执行代码会产生一个以候选为条件的运动序列，该序列与先前规划及记录的运动历史比较。输出是"执行后果 + 学习到的场景结果"的联合表示，用来刻画候选的未来，使规划器既能评估规划可能导向何处，也能评估车辆如何进入该未来；被选中的规划会进入下一次决策的执行上下文，从而在模型内部串联连续决策。摘要未报告代码的来源与生成方式、模型架构与训练细节。

title: MXI-MemICL: Towards In-Context Robot Manipulation through Self-Retrieved Interaction Memory
summary: In-context learning (ICL) offers robots a way to acquire new skills from a single demonstration without parameter updates. However, existing robotic ICL methods either rely on large-scale pretraining constrained by scarce, costly robot interaction data or require additional annotations yet struggle to generalize across tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose MXI-MemICL, a framework for memory-guided ICL in vision-language-action (VLA) models. By treating demonstrations as retrievable memory, MXI-MemICL enables in-context manipulation without additional large-scale pretraining or specialized annotations. Specifically, a visual-action causal encoder turns actions and their observed effects in demonstrations and completed interactions into reusable memory to guide execution. To retrieve experience suited to upcoming execution, an intention predictor forecasts the next stage's intent and uses it to query memory. The retrieved experience conditions the language backbone through experience-token prefixes and gated cross-attention, guiding action generation with a learned gate that regulates its influence. MXI-MemICL improves success over the baseline by +8.2% and +14.4% on RoboCasa365 and RoboTwin 2.0. Real-robot experiments show a +9.0% gain, with demonstrations adding +5.0% on seen and +16.7% on unseen tasks. The code will be made publicly available.

title: AirLeg: A Robust and Accurate Self-Supervised Visual-Inertial-Leg SLAM System
summary: Visual-inertial-leg (VIL) state estimation offers cost-effective localization for legged robots, adding only a camera to the onboard IMU and joint encoders. However, learning-based leg odometry is limited by its supervision: networks trained in simulation suffer from the sim-to-real gap, while real-world labels require costly sensors or inherit the errors of visual estimates. To address this, we present AirLeg, a self-supervised VIL SLAM system in which vision and leg proprioception improve each other from training to deployment. We pre-train the leg odometry network in simulation and adapt it to the robot without ground truth through imperative learning, where multi-sensor bundle adjustment uses the leg odometry to refine the visual map, which in turn supervises the network. During deployment, the fused estimates adapt the network online. To improve both localization and this supervision, a dual-window estimator fuses vision, IMU, and leg odometry, relates loaded feet to the visually reconstructed terrain through a deformation-aware constraint, and weights the constraints by variance component estimation. AirLeg completes all 17 GrandTour sequences with the lowest average error (0.19 m) among 19 methods. On a low-cost quadruped, it achieves the lowest drift (0.6%) with only 0.5 h of unlabeled data, in real time on an embedded computer.

AI.tldr: AirLeg 用"视觉与腿部本体感知互为监督"的自监督 VIL SLAM，在仿真预训练后无需真值即可适配真机；作者报告在 GrandTour 全部 17 条序列上平均误差 0.19 m（19 种方法中最低），低成本四足上漂移 0.6%。

title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
summary: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories. Building on Fast-WAM, which showed that video prediction shapes policy representations during training so that future frame synthesis can be skipped at deployment, we present G0.7, a generalist world action model scaled along two axes: extending the context window from a single observation to up to five minutes of history, and scaling pretraining to a large-scale corpus of robot teleoperation and human egocentric (ego) video. Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6x faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging.

AI.tldr: G0.7是一个通用world action model，把Fast-WAM的单帧观测上下文扩展到最长五分钟历史，并把预训练规模扩到机器人遥操作加人类第一视角视频；部署时直接解码动作（Fast模式）即可匹配IDM推理，单张RTX 5090 上每16步动作块耗时60 ms。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出两个具体缺口：world action models 虽能用视频生成器把视频中学到的物理先验迁移到操作策略，但每个动作前都先生成未来帧会让测试时推理慢到难以做闭环控制；同时多数现有策略只支持很短的观测历史。
AI.method: 输入是机器人观测历史（由单帧扩展到最长五分钟）和预训练数据（大规模机器人遥操作视频加人类egocentric视频）。方法沿用Fast-WAM的结论——视频预测的作用是训练时塑造策略表征，因此部署时可跳过未来帧生成——在此基础上做两个方向的放大：加长上下文窗口、放大预训练语料。输出是动作，可有两条推理路径：先想象再行动的IDM，或训练后直接解码动作的Fast模式；另有视频条件的in-context learning设定。

AI.conclusion: 对world models与机器人策略方向，本文给出的信号是：视频生成的价值可以主要落在训练期的表征塑造上，从而在部署时省掉逐动作的图像合成；长上下文与更大规模的人类/机器人视频预训练被作者报告为可同时支撑真机闭环部署与跨域泛化。证据边界是仅有摘要信息，未提供消融、计算开销曲线、baseline细节或统计检验，因此不能判断增益来自上下文长度、数据规模还是二者交互。

title: RoboDemo: Reconciling Demonstration Intent and Execution Progress for Long-Horizon Manipulation
summary: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires more than predicting the next action from the current observation. The policy must maintain a global procedural prior that specifies the expected progress of each subtask stage, while also tracking the realized progress produced by its interactions. To this end, we propose RoboDemo, a demonstration-augmented manipulation framework built on Dual-Cascaded Test-Time-Training. RoboDemo accepts either a task-relevant human demonstration video or a semantically compatible robot video retrieved from simulation corpus as reference, allowing us to evaluate its applicability with and without paired human demonstrations. Task semantics and physical motion information from the reference video are then transferred into persistent demonstration-intent memory. During deployment, we causally compress online observations, robot states, and executed actions into interaction-progress memory. To keep reference intent stable while interaction progress continually evolves, reference and execution video tokens independently update their respective fast-weight states. The action expert performs cascaded memory reads, first obtaining reference guidance and then refining it using realized progress, allowing the policy to adapt to execution deviations without overwriting the stored intent. RoboDemo achieves 90.7% success on Imitator Game and 73.3% success across three real-world household tasks. Real-world videos, code and hf-weights are available in our project website.

AI.tldr: 长时程操作需要同时维持全局子任务进度先验并追踪实际执行进度。RoboDemo 用双级联测试时训练，把参考视频的演示意图与在线交互进度分别存入两套快权重记忆，动作专家级联读取后输出动作；作者报告 Imitator Game 成功率 90.7%，三个真实家庭任务成功率 73.3%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出长时程机器人操作"不只是从当前观测预测下一动作"：策略既要维持描述各子任务阶段预期进度的全局程序先验，又要追踪自身交互产生的实际进度。二者需要同时满足，但摘要未报告既有方法在此处的具体失败数值。
AI.method: 输入可以是任务相关的人类演示视频，也可以是从仿真语料中检索出的语义兼容机器人视频，因此作者称可在有/无配对人类演示两种条件下评估适用性。方法把参考视频中的任务语义与物理运动信息转移进持久化的 demonstration-intent memory；部署阶段把在线观测、机器人状态与已执行动作因果压缩为 interaction-progress memory。参考视频 token 与执行视频 token 各自独立更新其快权重状态，使参考意图保持稳定而交互进度持续演化。动作专家的记忆读取是级联的：先取得参考引导，再用已实现的进度对其精化，从而在适应执行偏差的同时不覆盖已存意图。输出是动作策略。相对基线的具体对照在摘要中未报告。
AI.result: 作者报告两项成功率：Imitator Game 上 90.7%，三个真实家庭任务上 73.3%。摘要未给出基线名称或基线数值，也未报告相对提升幅度、百分比点差异、硬件、延迟或统计显著性，因此无法判断增益来源与量级。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义在于一种记忆组织方式：把"参考意图"与"执行进度"拆成两套独立演化的快权重状态，并用级联读取让策略在执行偏差下修正动作而不改写已存意图，这为长时程操作中先验与反馈的冲突提供了一种设计思路。证据边界很窄：摘要只报告两个成功率数值，未报告基线、消融、效率指标与失败分析，因此不能据此推断相对增益、跨任务泛化性或部署成本；真实机器人结果仅限摘要所述的三个家庭任务。

title: ViTacLab: Physically Consistent Visuo-Tactile Simulation, Benchmarking, and Representation Learning for Robotic Manipulation
summary: Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich robotic manipulation, but existing visuo-tactile simulators trade physical fidelity for scalability, and benchmarks largely focus on two-finger grippers. We present ViTacLab, a framework comprising ViTacSim, ViTacBench, and ViTacPolicy. ViTacSim uses a tri-modal tactile primitive: a global sparse contact-force lattice, a local dense force array, and tactile images. Anchored to PhysX contact-solver outputs, it corrects normal inconsistency through local stiffness alignment and reconstructs tangential forces under decoupled slip-stick regimes while preserving GPU parallelism. A joint projection preserves the sparse wrench and enforces local friction cones. ViTacBench spans parallel grippers, dexterous hands, and bimanual systems, with tasks ranging from vision-dominant to tactile-dominant regimes. ViTacPolicy aggregates variable numbers of heterogeneous tactile inputs using spatial-pose embeddings and a Transformer, and aligns force-array and tactile-image modalities through a two-stream VQ-VAE with a shared codebook. Controlled Hertzian-reference indentation and real-sensor sliding tests reduce normal and tangential force RMSE from 2.31 and 1.85 N to 0.42 and 0.53 N, respectively. Throughput reaches 2,482.9 tactile-pipeline FPS at 256 parallel environments. Simulation and real-world experiments show gains on several contact-rich tasks, while low absolute success on tactile-dominant tasks highlights the remaining difficulty of purely tactile control.

AI.tldr: 现有视触觉模拟器在物理保真与可扩展性之间取舍，且基准多限于两指夹爪。ViTacLab 统一了触觉仿真、跨本体基准与表征学习策略；摘要报告力RMSE显著下降、2,482.9 FPS吞吐，以及若干接触丰富任务的仿真与真机提升，但触觉主导任务绝对成功率仍低。
AI.motivation: 作者指出现有视触觉模拟器以牺牲物理保真换取可扩展性，同时基准主要覆盖两指夹爪，缺少对灵巧手与双臂系统的统一评测。摘要由此提出需要物理一致、可并行，并能覆盖多类操作本体与任务谱系的框架。
AI.method: 输入包括接触求解器输出、机器人/触觉配置，以及数量可变的异构触觉观测。ViTacSim 用三模态触觉原语表示接触：全局稀疏接触力格点、局部稠密力阵列和触觉图像；以 PhysX 接触求解器输出为锚，通过局部刚度对齐修正法向不一致，在解耦滑移—黏着机制下重建切向力，并做联合投影以保留稀疏力旋量、施加局部摩擦锥，同时保持 GPU 并行。ViTacBench 覆盖平行夹爪、灵巧手和双臂系统，任务从视觉主导延伸到触觉主导。ViTacPolicy 用空间位姿嵌入与 Transformer 聚合可变数量的异构触觉输入，并用共享码本的双流 VQ-VAE 对齐力阵列与触觉图像。输出是仿真触觉信号、基准任务与操作策略。
AI.result: 在受控 Hertzian 参考压入与真实传感器滑动测试中，法向和切向力 RMSE 从 2.31 N、1.85 N 降至 0.42 N、0.53 N；摘要未给出对比基线名称。触觉管线吞吐为 2,482.9 FPS（256 个并行环境）。仿真与真实实验在若干接触丰富任务上有提升，但摘要未报告具体任务、成功率数值和提升幅度；触觉主导任务绝对成功率仍低。
AI.conclusion: 该工作把物理一致的视触觉仿真、多本体基准与异构触觉表征学习放在同一框架中，摘要证据支持其在力重建精度、并行吞吐和若干操作任务上的收益。但策略性能仅有定性描述，触觉主导任务成功率仍低，且缺少具体基线数值与真机硬件细节；结论应限于作者摘要所述，不能据此推断已解决纯触觉控制或 sim-to-real 泛化。

title: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
summary: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables vision-language-action policies to improve through environmental interaction. However, in long-horizon manipulation, sparse success/failure feedback provides little information about where policies encounter bottlenecks. Moreover, repeated full-task rollouts also leave these bottlenecks weakly analyzed and insufficiently practiced. To this end, we introduce ReFocus, a progress-guided multi-round RL framework that alternates between Global and Local RL to identify task-specific bottlenecks and allocate additional practice to them. Specifically, during Global RL, we decompose each task into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of subtasks. Then a DAG-based Progress Reward is leveraged for both policy training and bottleneck diagnosis. Based on the identified bottlenecks, ReFocus selects Adaptive Practice Windows, defining task segments from an entry stage to a target stage. It allocates additional interaction to these segments during Local RL while updating the entire policy. After that, it evaluates the policy to perform the full task for the next round of RL, forming an iteration between Global and Local RL. Experiments on LIBERO-Long and RoboCasa365 show that ReFocus achieves success rates of 97.8% and 51.3%, respectively, compared with 90.6% and 39.3% for the $\pi_{0.5}$ baseline. Furthermore, we evaluate a real-world adaptation on three long-horizon tasks. On BreadBaker, ReFocus achieves 95% success, compared with 30% for the $\pi_{0.5}$. Project page: this https URL .
